facts.claim: Incentive to switch a home from oil (or propane) heat to electric heat. Amount depends on the technology, adjusted net income and household size. Can cover up to 100% of the cost. Paid directly to a participating installer.
facts.amount: Central heat pump: up to $22,000 income-qualified, up to $9,000 general. Multi-split or multiple mini-splits: up to $18,000 income-qualified, up to $6,500 general. Electric furnace or boiler: up to $10,000 income-qualified, up to $5,000 general.
facts.eligibility: If two technologies are installed, one incentive is paid for the higher-cost one. Income-qualified homeowners who already finished a Canada Greener Homes heat pump grant before April 1, 2023 cannot get a heat pump incentive. Income-qualified customers pre-approved for a central, multi-split or multiple mini-split heat pump also get a one-time $250 payment mailed by Natural Resources Canada.
facts.dates: Accepting applications on 2026-10-27 with no closing date set; the page says intake continues and applications are processed based on budget availability. Retroactive to projects completed after April 1, 2023.
facts.notes: Amount table is an image on the page (https://takechargenl.ca/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/INCENTIVES-CHART.png), read 2026-10-16. Delivered by takeCHARGE (Newfoundland Power and NL Hydro) with the federal and provincial governments. Installer sites say the $22,000 combines federal OHPA money (up to $15,000) and provincial money; not stated on the takeCHARGE page, so do not state the split.

facts.program: Oil to Electric Incentive Program income chart
facts.claim: Income-qualified stream limits by household size, using adjusted net income (line 23600 minus line 43500) of the homeowner and spouse or partner.
facts.amount: 1 person $37,375 or less; 2 persons $73,600; 3 persons $104,650; 4 persons $131,100; 5 or more persons $136,850. Above these: general stream.
facts.eligibility: Household counts homeowners (maximum two) plus anyone else living in the home year-round at application.

facts.program: Oil to Electric Incentive Program rules
facts.claim: Homeowner with an active electricity account; permanent foundation, primary residence, used year-round; new homes not eligible; connected to the island or Labrador interconnected grid. Oil homes need a 12-month oil statement within two years showing at least 500 litres (propane 1,000 litres). New oil tanks registered or installed since January 1, 2025 trigger extra review. Landlords can do up to two rental properties through the general stream.
facts.eligibility: Heat pumps must be air-source (mini-split, multi-split or central) listed by NRCan as OHPA-eligible for the climate zone, and must heat the whole house (installer signs an attestation; a single mini-split rarely qualifies). Central heat pumps need a sized, permanent, automatic backup. Baseboards only as backup. Covers panel upgrades where needed and oil tank removal. Must use an installer on the participating list (Journeyman refrigeration and air conditioning mechanic or manufacturer-certified). Quote with itemized costs needed to apply. Installers can invoice the utility directly for pre-approved customers.
facts.notes: Page warns that a heat pump without backup heat may void home insurance. Inquiries OiltoElectric@TakeChargeNL.ca; Newfoundland Power 1-800-663-2802; NL Hydro 1-888-737-1296.

facts.program: takeCHARGE insulation, duct insulation and HRV rebates
facts.claim: Extra takeCHARGE rebates listed for homes that switch from oil to electric heat.
facts.amount: Attic insulation 75% up to $1,000; basement insulation 75% up to $1,000; up to $1,000 more toward labour for both areas with a participating professional installer; duct insulation 50% up to $500; qualifying HRV $225.
facts.eligibility: Listed on the Oil to Electric page as programs you can qualify for after switching to electric heat. Must qualify.
facts.notes: Full rules for each rebate are on their own takeCHARGE pages, not read yet.

facts.program: Home Heating Supplement Program (furnace and stove oil), Government of Newfoundland and Labrador
facts.claim: Supplement for residents who directly pay for furnace or stove oil to heat their principal residence. The 2026 program was enhanced: the maximum rose from $500 to $1,000 and the minimum from $200 to $400. Residents who already applied do not need to apply again; those already paid get a second payment later this year.
facts.eligibility: 2025 adjusted family income of $150,000 or less, with 2025 tax return filed with the CRA. $1,000 maximum where income is $100,000 or less; partial supplement (minimum $400) above $100,000 up to $150,000. Invoices for at least 250 litres of furnace or stove oil bought Jan 1 to Dec 31, 2026, in the applicant's or spouse's name and address. One person per household. Heat included in rent and fully subsidized NL Housing units are not eligible without invoices.
facts.dates: Open for applications until January 15, 2027. Late applications are not accepted. Most applications processed within 10 weeks.
facts.notes: Read directly on the program page 2026-10-27 (it supersedes the July 16 news release, which said $200 to $500). Apply online (HHSP Online page), by the 2026 application form, or by mail to Home Heating Supplement Program, Department of Finance, P.O. Box 8700, St. John's, NL A1B 4J6. Paper forms at Finance and SeniorsNL (St. John's), Jobs, Growth and Rural Development offices, Government Service Centres (not Springdale or Lewisporte) and public libraries. Payment by direct deposit if the CRA refund or GST/HST credit goes that way, else cheque. Help: OilSupplement@gov.nl.ca, 709-729-4645, toll-free 1-844-729-4645. How the partial amount is worked out between $100,000 and $150,000 is not published.

facts.claim: On October 3, 2026, furnace oil in St. John's cost $2.16 per litre, almost a dollar more than on the same day in 2025. A 900-litre tank cost about $1,950 to fill, about $2,240 with taxes.
facts.notes: Canadian Press / CTV reporting, not an official price series. Article also reports the province promising a 15% electricity bill cut if the Churchill Falls deal is finalized: not confirmed, do not state as a rebate.

facts.claim: Rebate for attic and basement insulation in electrically heated homes.
facts.amount: 75% of cost up to $1,000 attic and $1,000 basement, plus up to $500 labour each area with a participating professional installer (up to $3,000 total)
facts.eligibility: Primary heat must be electric (or at least 15,000 kWh a year if another source is used). Home built and connected before January 1, 2014. Homeowner with active electricity account, permanent foundation, primary residence. Must reach minimum R-value; top-ups only, no full replacement (removed attic insulation counted from R20). Spray foam by participating installer. Pre-tax insulation and labour only. Paid as a bill credit.

facts.claim: Three air sealing pathways for electrically heated homes; all need an HRV or air exchanger.
facts.eligibility: Existing home: pre and post blower door tests, at least 10% ACH50 improvement ($200 at 10%, $475 at 20%, $750 at 30%+). With attic insulation replacement: $0.50 per sq ft sealed up to $750, homes built before 2014, paid to the installer. New construction: 2.5 ACH50 or less, $200 to $750, within 12 months of occupancy permit. Primary heat electric (or 15,000 kWh minimum).

facts.claim: Rebate on an eligible high-efficiency HRV (some ERVs) installed by an HRAI certified installer.
facts.eligibility: Any heat source. Homeowner with active electricity account, permanent foundation. Model must be on takeCHARGE's eligible list. Bill credit, up to eight weeks.
facts.notes: $225 amount read on the Oil to Electric page (nl-3); HRV page states the rules.

facts.claim: Duct insulation on primary heating ducts in unheated areas.
facts.eligibility: Primary heat is an electric furnace or central ducted heat pump (or 15,000 kWh minimum). R-6 to R-8 duct wrap or sleeve on the outside of ducts. Material only, no labour. Bought on or after September 26, 2022.

facts.claim: Income-eligible program with the Government of Canada: a limited number of no-cost heat pumps, HRVs, insulation and air sealing upgrades and home energy assessments. Incentives can cover up to 100% of the cost.
facts.amount: up to 100% of eligible upgrade cost
facts.eligibility: Same income chart as Oil to Electric (1 person $37,375 ... 5+ $136,850). Homeowners and landlords (max two properties; tenants must be income-eligible, 12 months rental history, consent). Island or Labrador interconnected grid; isolated diesel communities apply and Hydro staff follow up. New homes not eligible. Steps: apply, energy assessment, contractor quotes approved by TakeCharge, work, post inspection; TakeCharge pays contractors and auditors.
facts.notes: Help: Newfoundland Power 1-800-663-2802 greenerhomes@takechargenl.ca; NL Hydro 1-888-737-1296 greenerhomes@nlh.nl.ca.

facts.program: On-bill financing, HESP and St. John's Shift
facts.claim: Newfoundland Power and NL Hydro offer on-bill financing for heat pumps and insulation (Newfoundland Power also thermostats, HRVs, electric water heaters and more). NL Housing's Home Energy Savings Program (HESP) helps low-income households using 15,000 kWh a year with retrofits. econext and the City of St. John's run Shift, free guidance for energy renovations.
facts.eligibility: Financing amounts and terms not read on the utility pages: do not state them. takeCHARGE's residential rebate list shows no heat pump rebate for homes already heated by electricity.

facts.claim: Newfoundland Power is the primary distributor of electricity on the island portion of Newfoundland and Labrador, owned by Fortis Inc.
facts.eligibility: Some island customers are served by NL Hydro instead; check your bill.

facts.claim: Newfoundland and Labrador Hydro serves customers in Labrador City and Wabush (Labrador West), supplied over transmission lines from Churchill Falls; Labrador City can get backup power when those lines are down.
facts.notes: Whether every Labrador West home counts as on the 'Labrador interconnected grid' for Oil to Electric is not stated: tell readers to confirm with Hydro.
